content.value_statement: TypeScript projects often lose safety through loose state models and duplicated runtime contracts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward type-first patterns that reduce invalid states.
actual_capabilities: Recommends discriminated unions for mutually exclusive application states.
Shows branded types for domain identifiers and primitive values.
Promotes const assertions for synchronized runtime arrays and literal unions.
Guides exhaustive switch handling with never checks.
Explains Zod schemas for runtime validation and inferred TypeScript types.
Points to type-fest utilities for advanced type modeling.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not run TypeScript compilers or tests.
React-specific patterns are delegated to a separate React skill.
It does not cover framework-specific build systems or deployment workflows.
Examples may need adaptation for existing codebase conventions.

use_cases.title: Model safer async state
use_cases.description: Convert boolean-heavy request state into discriminated unions that prevent invalid combinations.

use_cases.title: Validate API boundaries
use_cases.description: Use Zod schemas to parse external data and infer matching TypeScript types.

use_cases.title: Review type design
use_cases.description: Check TypeScript code for missing brands, incomplete switch handling, and duplicated schema definitions.

prompt_templates.title: Review a TypeScript file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript file for type-safety improvements. Focus on discriminated unions, branded identifiers, and obvious runtime validation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Improve runtime validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this API boundary to use Zod as the source of truth. Infer TypeScript types from the schema and explain any tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Harden domain models
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these domain types for invalid states. Propose branded types, literal unions, and exhaustive checks where they improve correctness.

prompt_templates.title: Design a type strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript type-safety strategy for this module. Include compile-time modeling, runtime validation, error handling, and utility type recommendations.

output_examples.input: A request state object uses loading, data, and error fields together.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a discriminated union with idle, loading, success, and error variants so impossible combinations cannot compile.

output_examples.input: An API response is cast directly to a User type.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests validating the response with a Zod schema and deriving the User type from that schema.

output_examples.input: A switch statement handles known statuses but has no default safety check.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends an exhaustive never check so new statuses produce compile-time failures until handled.

best_practices: Use discriminated unions to represent mutually exclusive states.
Keep runtime schemas and TypeScript types in sync through inference.
Add exhaustive never checks when branching over finite unions.
anti_patterns: Do not model exclusive states with unrelated boolean flags.
Do not duplicate runtime schemas and TypeScript interfaces by hand.
Do not cast external data to trusted types without validation.

faq.question: Does this skill execute TypeScript code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for improving TypeScript and JavaScript code.

faq.question: Can it help with React components?
faq.answer: It can help with TypeScript parts of React files, but React-specific guidance should use the companion React skill.

faq.question: Does it require Zod?
faq.answer: No. Zod is recommended for runtime validation examples, but projects can adapt the guidance to other validators.

faq.question: Is it useful for JavaScript files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide safer patterns in JavaScript projects that use TypeScript annotations, gradual migration, or shared models.

faq.question: Does it replace tests?
faq.answer: No. It improves type modeling and validation, but tests are still needed for behavior and integration coverage.

faq.question: What tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
